fields.System.Title: OUT-7 — Order status projection
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Answer "where is order 12345?" in one read instead of a five-table join.

Scope

In. Maintaining the order_status projection and exposing a tracking endpoint.

Out. Customer-facing tracking pages. This provides the data.

Design notes

The honest query joins order, allocation, pick task, carton, and shipment. Customer service
asks it constantly, and it is one of the first queries to become slow.

Update it asynchronously from events. Unlike availability, order status tolerates a few
seconds of staleness — nobody is making a promise based on it. That keeps the update off the
hot dispatch transaction.

Expose last_updated_at. A customer service agent who can see the status is four hours old
will check elsewhere. One who cannot will confidently quote stale information.

Build the rebuild job with the projection. Same rule as
[INV-9](../INV/INV-9-availability-projection.md) — during an incident you need to run it, not
write it.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Projection drifts from source | [doc 08 §10](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| No rebuild job exists | [doc 08 §3](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
| Staleness invisible to the reader | [doc 08 §5.3](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md) |
